newsitem.title: UK: Freight market still hesitant after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Freight market still hesitant after holidays.

text.p: The freight market lacks shape following the holiday season and the absence of reported business has made most brokers cautious about forecasting market trends.
The situation was reflected by today's Baltic Freight Index, down one point to 1510.

GRAIN - Rumours that Geepee had fixed Caper tonnage for barley from US Gulf and/or the Continent to Saudi Arabia were denied by sources close to the charterers. Toepfer meannwhile still quoted 75,000 barley from Rouen and Dunkirk to Saudi Arabia for Jan 8/14.

Continental were believed to have fixed a Panamax for a transatlantic round with grain to east Med including Israel, possibly the 1976-built Van Ommeren-relet Sarah 72,000 dwt. Continental also booked Chinese tonnage for 30,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Indonesia for Jan 17/25 at close to $34.00.

Brokers said Toepfer fixed Chusovoy for about 31,000 grains 55' US Gulf/Spain loading next week at a lumpsum equivalent of $17.50 and are in the market with a new order for 1.2/1.6m cft US Gulf/Ireland for prompt shipment.
Dreyfus were reported to be on subjects for 20,000 wheat Rouen/West Italy for prompt loading at $12.50.

New business quoted today included Andre with 20,000 wheat up River/Labuan and Kuching and 25,000 wheat up River/Port Sudan, both for Jan 17/25. Elsewhere Continental quoted 54,300 heavy grain Nopac/Taiwan for Jan 21/Feb 1 and 30,000 heavy grain on the same route for Feb 1/10.

Noble were reported to have booked China Spirit 70,070 dwt delivery Japan retro end Dec for a trip via Nopac to Bin Qasim at $10,900 daily, and Pan Ocean were said to have covered a locally-controlled Panamax for W.Australia/Bin Qasim on private terms.

MINERALS - The Caper market has hardly recovered from the holiday break. A few non-grain Panamax fixtures were rumoured - the Hanjin-relet Deerpool 65,163 dwt for Tampa/China fertilizers for mid Jan, possibly at only $25.50, for example, and Mariann 64,064 dwt or a trip far east - but little else was heard. Brokers reported further demand for Panamaxes from Australia.

HANDY-SIZES - Smaller types of geared tonnage were said to be struggling in all areas except Brazil and Argentina. Severe weather conditions have disrupted demand for this category of vessel from the Continent.

Reports surfaced of short period fixtures of Handymaxes said to have been concluded by T K Boesun last month - the newbuilding Pacific Scorpio 49,000 dwt delivery-yard Japan mid Jan for 6 option 6 months in the $9,000's daily, and Irene 43,000 dwt delivery far East for 3-5 months in the mid-$8,000's daily.
Irene is understood to have been relet to Western Bulkcarriers for a trip from S.Australia to Saudi Arabia.
